articles.title: 'Spoke brilliantly' but Liverpool fans torn on Mac Allister contract comments
articles.summary: Alexis Mac Allister splits opinion on his public comments regarding his contract at Liverpool, as fans and BBC Sport pundit Pat Nevin share opinions.
body: Did Alexis Mac Allister strike the right tone when he told the media about his contract situation with Liverpool?

The Argentine midfielder has a deal with the Reds until 2028, but said on Tuesday that he is "very sad" not to have received a new contract in the summer after team-mates Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch penned new agreements.
The public approach to stalling contract dealings is nothing new at Liverpool.
In November 2024, Mohamed Salah spoke openly about his contract stalemate when he admitted he was "disappointed" by a lack of offers from the club, as he entered the final six months of his deal.

articles.title: Circus or spectacular? Either way, NFL’s exercise in cultural exchange has gripped Melbourne | Jack Snape
articles.summary: Friday’s game between the 49ers and Rams at the MCG is almost sold out with millions more set to watch on Netflix. The assembled press kept asking, but the American would not give them what they wanted. Just what does San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan think of Melbourne?
body: “I haven’t left the hotel, except to come to this practice, for five days or however long we’ve been here,” he said at a training session on Wednesday, admitting to jet lag that has woken him at 1am all week.
Australians relish what the rest of the world thinks of them, perhaps none more than Melburnians. Of their coffee. Of their status as the country’s so-called sporting capital.

“I would love to say I’m getting out and experiencing Australia and I’m sure if I did, I’d think it’s awesome,” Shanahan continued, trying to maintain the spirit of this vast exercise in cultural exchange. “But this is just … we travel a lot, and when we do, we don’t really do anything.”

Fortunately, there are many Americans happy to express their views. The travelling NFL media contingent have been doing the heavy lifting, espousing opinions on local cuisine and lifestyle difference. Some, like Grant Cohn, have brought their brash approach to tongue-in-cheek coverage of local sport; he called for the Western Bulldogs to trade Marcus Bontempelli.

articles.title: Carrick up for ‘magical’ Champions League but derby timing ‘not ideal’
articles.summary: United play Sabah, then Manchester City on Sunday. ‘To win the Champions League was the ultimate’ Michael Carrick is excited to lead Manchester United on their return to the “magical” Champions League but admitted playing on Thursday night was “not ideal” with the derby on Sunday.
body: United welcome Sabah to Old Trafford after a two-year Champions League absence. The Azerbaijani club are making their debut among Europe’s elite, having been in existence for less than a decade.

“It’s a magical competition,” Carrick, who won the competition in 2008 with United, said. “It’s where we all want to be. When you’re out of it, you realise how special it is, and when you’re in it, you want to make the most of it. I think we’ve all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years.

“It’s where we want to be, it’s what we want to get back to, and it’s the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best. We’re delighted to be here, but we’re not here to just enjoy the occasion. We’re here to do business and go as far as we possibly can.
“To win the Champions League for me was the ultimate and was the best feeling I’ve had. Be nice some day to feel that again.”

articles.title: 'I'm not a robot' - Kerr responds to criticism before Ingebrigtsen reunion
articles.summary: Josh Kerr says he is "very happy" to see Jakob Ingebrigtsen back competing - but he is "not going to lose" when they resume their fierce rivalry this weekend.
body: Their long-established war of words was recently reignited when Ingebrigtsen criticised Kerr's decision to miss last month's European Championships, where the Norwegian marked his return from long-term injury by winning 5,000m gold.

The men's 1500m at the inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest this weekend will have added edge after Ingebrigtsen, 25, labelled his rivals a "bunch of cowards" at last week's Diamond League Final.

Speaking to the media before the championship, Kerr was reluctant to directly address Ingebrigtsen's recent comments towards him but admitted their presence would bring "a lot more energy" to the event.
"When you boil it down, I'm very happy that he's back racing," said Kerr, 28.

articles.title: Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: Fantasy Advice for Your Broncos Players in Week 1
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season kicks off later tonight with a Super Bowl rematch (it should have included the Broncos) between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots. That also means the 2026 fantasy football season is underway, and I am here to tell you which Denver Broncos players you should…
body: The Broncos cap off the start of Week 1 with a key AFC West divisional showdown against the returning quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. The Broncos will also have their quarterback, Bo Nix, returning from offseason ankle surgery and will be debuting explosive wide receiver and big offseason addition, Jaylen Waddle.
So, with all that said, here are the Denver Broncos players I believe you should start or sit during Week 1 of the 2026 fantasy football season.

Nix has had success vs. the Chiefs throughout his career. He has a 3-1 record vs. them and would be undefeated if it were not for a blocked game-winning field goal. Nix also has a passer rating of 108.8 with 1,013 yards, 7 touchdowns, and 1 interception in 4 games against the Chiefs in his career.

Now, add Jaylen Waddle, an improved Pat Bryant, a strong running game, and Davis Webb calling the offense. This will be the strongest supporting cast Nix has ever had with the Broncos, and this offense is ready to take that next step.

articles.summary: The only thing gloomier than the leaden skies at lunch on day of the third Test at Edgbaston will be the mood in the Pakistan dressing room as things went from bad to worse.

Former Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja said Pakistan's "technique and mindset" were "pretty ordinary".

articles.title: José Mourinho weighs in on Trent Alexander-Arnold's midfield stint in Champions League win
articles.summary: José Mourinho maintains that Trent Alexander-Arnold is "not a midfielder" despite utilizing the ex-Liverpool player in that central role on Tuesday. 'The Special One' extended his encouraging beginning to his second tenure at the Santiago Bernabéu as Real Madrid defeated another of his former…
body: Mourinho was lacking midfield choices due to suspensions for Eduardo Camavinga, Arda Güler, and Bernardo Silva, which led him to think outside the box and deploy Alexander-Arnold alongside Federico Valverde in the engine room. The former Liverpool star featured in that position during his youth and has also filled that role with England on previous occasions.

Gareth Southgate utilized him there during Euro 2024 before abandoning the trial after just two group stage matches while, throughout his Liverpool tenure, he frequently advanced into midfield, albeit from his right-back slot, and Mourinho evidently views him as a full-back, as per The Mirror.

The Portuguese manager commented: "He has played midfield with England and Liverpool... but he is not a midfielder. He has played very well. He has interpreted what he needed to really well, tactically. Both him and Valverde have worked very well at this level."

Alexander-Arnold created two chances and attempted more crosses than any other Real player during his time in midfield, yet failed to win a single tackle. His passing accuracy also dipped to 83.3 percent, something Mourinho attributed to the positional adjustment.

articles.title: Merson: Arsenal didn't make X-factor signing to win Champions League
articles.summary: Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level.
body: They have enough to win the Premier League with their squad. I just think the forward line against the big boys, they're missing that little ingredient.
If they'd had a Vinicius Junior or a Julian Alvarez, that would have given them the edge to go on and win the Champions League.

I'm a big fan of Kai Havertz. He does a lot of work and he's what I call a good footballer. He works hard and makes the right decisions. I just think he's not going to score 20 goals in a season. To take them to the Premier League title, there's no doubt about it, he's a top-drawer player.

The other thing I look at is when Arsenal go and play against Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, teams like that in the Champions League latter stages, the centre-halves and the full-backs, getting up in the morning and going to their team talk and saying to one of the other players, "Didn't sleep very well last night, a bit worried about who I'm playing against".

articles.title: 'It’s about finding a way to get better': HC aims to fix red zone woes
articles.summary: Jennifer Toland's weekly area college football notes looks HC's red zone woes, Bob Chesney's debut at UCLA and a stellar start for a St. Paul star.
body: Holy Cross has started the 2026 season 0-2 – more critically, 0-2 in the Patriot League – following back-to-back 35-10 losses to Lehigh and Colgate, but coach Dan Curran said the Crusaders are regrouping, continuing to show great discipline and effort, and looking forward to this week’s challenge at FBS opponent Miami University in Oxford, Ohio.
“It’s about finding a way to get better every single week,” Curran said. “The guys are excited about this opportunity.”

Curran pointed to tackling and red zone woes as two of the biggest issues in the Lehigh game. Against the Raiders, it was pass defense, continued struggles in the red zone and the inability to establish the run game.

Colgate quarterback Jake Stearney completed eight pass attempts of 18 yards or longer. His first-quarter touchdown throws, to cap consecutive series, went for 33 and 64 yards, and he had a 58-yarder in the third.

articles.title: Leeds full-back Miller ruled out of Super League play-offs
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos will be without Lachie Miller for the Super League play-offs after head coach Brad Arthur revealed the star full-back will be sidelined for 10 to 12 weeks, due to a torn hamstring.
body: Miller, who has been one of Leeds' most crucial attackers this season, sustained the injury during the early stages of his side's 40-8 defeat to Wigan Warriors on Saturday.
Arthur confirmed the news on Wednesday, adding the 32-year-old will fortunately not require surgery to remedy the injury.
It is a huge blow for Miller and Leeds, who was a firm favourite to be crowned this season's Man of Steel, ranking third for the most metres and the most carries.
The Rhinos boss also revealed the surprising news that Ash Handley would step in at full-back for the injured Miller for his side's final regular-season Super League clash against Hull FC on Friday.

articles.title: Korda plays down 'intimidation factor' as Hull eyes rematch with world No 1
articles.summary: Charley Hull said she would relish another Solheim Cup showdown with Nelly Korda, who played down bringing an "intimidation factor" to Team Europe.
body: Hull makes an eighth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance for Team Europe, who look to regain the trophy at Bernardus Golf - live on Sky Sports - after losing on American soil two years ago.

The 30-year-old top-scored for Team Europe in their 2024 defeat and despatched Korda 6&4 during the Sunday singles, with Hull open to facing the world No 1 again for Anna Nordqvist's side during their pursuit of a home victory.
"Playing Nelly Korda at that time was really good - it was so much fun," Hull said in her pre-tournament press conference. "I came out and played pretty well.
"Every dog has its day and I also did that day, but she's had a pretty incredible season so far this year. If it came down to singles, it would be a really good match.
